content.overview: Epistolary jurisdiction allows the court to treat a letter or informal communication as a writ petition where the writer lacks means or access to counsel and alleges serious public or fundamental-rights wrongs, subject to screening for genuineness.
content.study: PIL is a rule of standing, not a new writ. Epistolary practice (letters treated as petitions) grew to aid the poor and imprisoned; courts may convert correspondence into proceedings under Articles 32 or 226 after verifying bona fides. It does not license anonymous or motivated campaigns. Private disputes dressed as PIL fail; abuse and costs are dealt with under limits-and-costs.
